name: NS-2359
summary: NS-2359 (GSK-372475) is a serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor. It was under development by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) as an antidepressant, but was discontinued in 2009 when phase II clinical trials showed the drug was not effective and not well tolerated. The results did not support further effort by the company.

pharmacology.text: NS-2359 (GSK-372475) is a serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor.

uses.text: It was under development by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) as an antidepressant, but was discontinued in 2009 when phase II clinical trials showed the drug was not effective and not well tolerated. NS-2359 was also in clinical trials for the treatment of ADHD, phase II having been completed in 2007. A phase I clinical trial exploring the effect of NS-2359 on cocaine-dependent individuals was completed in 2002.

fact.en: It blocks the reuptake of all three monoamines at once, like cocaine does, but much more slowly, which was the idea behind testing it for cocaine addiction as well as depression.
fact.zh: 它像古柯鹼一樣同時阻斷三種單胺的再回收，但速度慢得多，這正是它除了憂鬱症之外，也被用於古柯鹼成癮試驗的原因。
fact.zhHans: 它像古柯碱一样同时阻断三种单胺的再回收，但速度慢得多，这正是它除了忧郁症之外，也被用于古柯碱成瘾试验的原因。
